edit.description: `flume loop` takes `loop.pid` through the shared stake; the hand-rolled probe-then-write and its `lockHeld` flag go
the refusal over a live holder and the reclaim over a dead one, through the stake

summary: `flume loop` probes `loop.pid` then writes it, so two starts can both read no holder and the second silently overwrites the first's claim

per.section: The loop lock and the tip claim

acceptance: the loop lock is acquired by the same exclusive-create stake the tip and entry claims use, so the section's refusal holds under a race; the refusal still names the holder's pid and an unreadable lock still exits EX_IOERR
pins: a loop start over a live loop.pid is refused naming the holder's pid
a loop start over a loop.pid whose recorded pid is dead reclaims the lock
a loop start over an unreadable loop.pid refuses with the io-error exit code
notes: Per note A-RELEASED-CLAIM-NEVER-UNLINKS-A-LATER-HOLDERS. The loop lock is the third guard writing `renderPidClaim` and the only one not on `stakePidClaim` (`src/pidClaim.ts`) — `.claude/rules/engineering.md`, *The fix lands at the mechanism*. `held.by.pid` is all the refusal message needs. No `tests[]`: the window is a two-process race the default lane cannot drive, and the observable contract is unchanged.
